questions.text: In this lesson, what does the European term “New World” refer to?
choices: The Asian trading regions Europeans hoped to reach
The African ports used on routes toward Asia
The European kingdoms sponsoring ocean voyages
questions.solution: Europeans used “New World” for the Americas. Indigenous peoples had lived there long before these European voyages.
questions.hint: Think about whose point of view made these lands seem “new.”
questions.source: NPS: Prelude to Jamestown; TCI published topic outline

questions.text: Which instrument used the angle of the sun or stars to help sailors estimate latitude?
choices: A map showing coastlines and possible sailing routes
A ship’s log recording cargo and daily voyage events
A magnetic compass that indicated a ship’s heading
questions.solution: An astrolabe helped measure the angle of a visible heavenly body. Sailors could use that information to estimate latitude.
questions.hint: Latitude means position north or south of the equator.
questions.source: NPS: Navigating the Atlantic World

questions.text: In 2.200, what is the value of the digit 2 in the tenths place?
questions.solution: The tenths place is 1 place to the right of the decimal point. 2 tenths = 0.2.
questions.hint: Name each place as you move right from the decimal point.

questions.text: Round EACH number to the nearest whole number, then estimate the sum.
questions.solution: 2.38 rounds to 2 and 2.64 rounds to 3. Estimate: 2 + 3 = 5.
questions.hint: Look at the tenths digit to round each number first.

question.text: In 2.200, what is the value of the digit 2 in the tenths place?
question.solution: The tenths place is 1 place to the right of the decimal point. 2 tenths = 0.2.
question.hint: Name each place as you move right from the decimal point.

questions.text: Calculate 1.2 × 2.
questions.solution: 1.2 × 2 = 2.4. Multiply 12 × 2 = 24; the factors have 1 decimal places in all. Divide that whole-number product by 10 and keep all places.
questions.hint: Think of equal groups. Multiply the digits and preserve the value of each decimal place.
questions.source: Provisional family-approved scope; 5.NBT.B.7. Chapter 4 contents unverified.

questions.text: Calculate 2.5 × 0.3.
questions.solution: 2.5 × 0.3 = 0.75. Multiply 25 × 03 = 75; the factors have 2 decimal places in all. Divide that whole-number product by 100 and keep all places.
questions.hint: Tenths times tenths give hundredths. Count places in both factors, then check the size.
questions.source: Provisional family-approved scope; 5.NBT.B.7. Chapter 4 contents unverified.

questions.text: A squad pours sand and steel paperclips into one supply tray. Why is this a mixture?
questions.answer: Two substances are combined and keep their original properties
choices: Two substances are combined and keep their original properties
Every combination forms a new substance
questions.solution: The sand is still sand, and the steel paperclips still have their own properties. Combining materials can make a mixture without a chemical change.
questions.hint: Ask whether the original materials keep their own properties.

questions.text: Why do pots and pans often have plastic or wooden handles?
questions.answer: Plastic and wood slow heat transfer toward the handle
choices: Plastic conducts heat better than metal
Plastic and wood slow heat transfer toward the handle
They make the pan cook faster
questions.solution: Plastic and wood are poor thermal conductors. They slow heat transfer compared with metal, so the handle warms more slowly.
questions.hint: A thermal conductor transfers heat more easily than an insulator.
